mainEntity.name: MyEllevate® or a neck lift: how do I know which?

acceptedAnswer.text: A neck lift uses small incisions behind the ears and under the chin and can last up to ten years. MyEllevate® places internal sutures through small punctures and lasts around five. MyEllevate® suits earlier laxity; a neck lift reverses more advanced sagging. MyEllevate® also needs only local anaesthetic, so you can drive yourself home.

mainEntity.name: Will a neck lift fix my jowls?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Jowls sit low on the face but originate in sagging facial tissue, so they are addressed in a facelift rather than a neck lift. A minimally invasive facelift is the procedure that reduces them.

Fillers are gel injectables that plump and smooth lines, acne scars and thin lips, lasting months to a couple of years. Facial implants are customised inserts made from a biocompatible material that stays intact, so the contour is permanent. Filler changes the surface; an implant changes the underlying structure.

mainEntity.name: How long does each result last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Blepharoplasty 10–15 years or more. A neck lift up to ten years. MyEllevate® around five. Facial implants and buccal fat reduction are permanent, though significant weight gain can return fullness elsewhere in the cheek. Injectables last months rather than years.

mainEntity.name: Can I have more than one procedure at once?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, and it is frequently the better plan. A neck lift can be performed alongside a facelift or eyelid surgery in one procedure, with a single recovery. What can be combined safely depends on your anatomy and time under anaesthetic, so it is decided at the consultation.

mainEntity.name: Why do some treatments not show a price?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because the practice never published a figure for those. Genioplasty, fat transfer and facelift fees vary genuinely with the case. Every other fee shown is the practice's own published price, currently being reconfirmed for 2026.
